key_insight: VOID enables physically plausible video object removal by not only filling pixels behind removed objects but also correcting downstream interactions (e.g., collisions, pushed objects) so post-edit dynamics look realistic.
problem_solved: Current video object removal models handle appearance-level inpainting (background, shadows, reflections) but fail when the removed object caused physical interactions with other scene elements, producing implausible or inconsistent motion and geometry after removal.
method: Create paired training data that simulates object removals along with the resulting interaction effects (e.g., collisions, displacement) so the model learns how scenes should evolve after deletion.

Joint model that combines interaction-aware dynamics prediction (to infer how other objects should move or settle) with temporal, occlusion- and flow-aware video inpainting to produce consistent frames.
Train with losses enforcing temporal consistency, physical-plausibility (e.g., motion/occlusion constraints), and high-fidelity appearance reconstruction to reconcile dynamics and visual realism.
impact: VOID makes video editing and removal robust in realistic, dynamic scenes where objects interact—improving quality for special-effects, content creation, and dataset curation. Practitioners gain a tool to produce coherent temporal edits that respect physical scene behavior.
visual_elements: Before/after frame sequence highlighting a removed object and corrected interaction (e.g., object collision undone and displaced item returned to plausible position).

paper_title: VOID: Video Object and Interaction Deletion
paper_authors: Saman Motamed, William Harvey, Benjamin Klein, Luc Van Gool, Zhuoning Yuan
